direction.premise: A silent glass-and-ceramic laboratory instrument where the phone itself becomes a maze under a rolling glass marble, driven by its actual tilt sensor.
direction.composition: The playable maze fills the physical glass edge of the viewport, with only three small instrument readouts around the perimeter and a separate brass-like control plate on pause.
direction.shapeLanguage: Straight ceramic border walls and narrow chamfered maze corners organize the space; the rolling sphere, recessed brass goal and sparse instrument marks create the recognizable silhouette.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: A physically shaded WebGL2 glass marble refracts and reflects ceramic barriers, with synthetic contact shadows and a Canvas 2D fallback preserving navigation on limited GPUs.
direction.paletteLogic: Deep green-black surrounds restrained cream ceramic and aged brass. Small luminous highlights identify the real transparent sphere and goal, without colorful HUD rectangles over the maze.
direction.typography: Narrow spaced instrument legends and tabular numerical stopwatch digits signal measured motion, while menu typography uses large serif lettering as an engraved instrument plate.
direction.signature: The maze touches the device bezel and the glass marble responds to the phone's actual tilt, with calibrated sensor controls and a live physical glass resonance following the motion.
direction.distinction: Unlike top-down Perekos combat and Rivals Field Notes statistics, ОТВЕС is one physical instrument without a virtual thumbstick or a scrolling chapter interface.

architecture.primaryVerb: Tilt the actual phone or drag its maze surface to roll the glass marble around obstacles and into the recessed goal hole while preserving progress on rotation.
architecture.physicalFeedback: Acceleration integrates the calibrated tilt into marble velocity and rolling orientation; physical wall contact triggers a short glass resonance and vibrations, and the goal locks the final falling animation.
architecture.spatialRationale: The maze covers the usable portrait or landscape screen while safe-area-aware time, pause and calibration controls stay at the edges; the play field retains full touch area and camera safe-fit prevents cropping when rotating an existing run.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Rivals Field Notes is an editorial document with permanent chapter navigation and evidence tables; ОТВЕС uses a single edge-to-edge ceramic maze with only a tiny time readout and an overlay pause plate.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Rivals Field Notes filters static season records, while ОТВЕС applies accelerometer or pointer tilt to inertial marble physics and responds to impacts.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Perekos places two visible spellcasters and two touch decks on a pixel-art arena; ОТВЕС has one glass marble and a closed ceramic maze that reaches the screen bezel without combat HUDs.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Perekos synchronizes competitive movement and casts timed spells; ОТВЕС calibrates physical tilt, rolls a sphere into the brass goal and records completion time.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Crumple Yard centers damageable vehicles in a driving ground environment with pedal controls; ОТВЕС fills the device with a compact static ceramic maze and hides all virtual driving decks.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Crumple Yard accelerates vehicles into impact damage, while ОТВЕС manipulates gravitational tilt and resolves marble contact and a timed goal capture.

production.renderer: A separate WebGL2 canvas shades 3D glass, ceramics and the goal with bounded optical buffers, while Canvas 2D on the original input surface remains an always-playable fallback.
production.focalAsset: The highly transparent rolling marble inside a nearly bezel-to-bezel ceramic maze is the central interactive object, generated as deterministic geometry with a recessed goal.

motion.character: The sphere exhibits inertial rolling and collisions instead of spring animation, with gentle visual tilt changing reflections but never artificially shaking the camera.
motion.action: Tilt the phone to move the marble through a narrow corridor and release the input before the recessed brass finish hole.
motion.anticipation: The live sensor status and the visible upcoming wall signal what acceleration will do; the marble remains motionless until an actual tilt or touch input arrives.
motion.response: The marble begins accelerating under the recalibrated gravity component on the next physics tick and its rotational shading changes with rolling velocity.
motion.followThrough: After finger release the marble keeps its inertial velocity, slows from friction, collides with walls and falls visibly into the goal when captured.
motion.interruption: A reverse tilt or rapid finger change immediately changes acceleration while preserving inertia; pause freezes the physics and re-calibration moves the neutral tilt reference.
motion.reducedMotion: Reduced motion removes decorative menu animation while the stopwatch, visible wall contact, marble positions and full maze still convey physical motion and progress.

evidence.expectedChange: Pressing the start control hides the instrument title plate and reveals the full working WebGL or Canvas maze, running timer and moving physical marble.
